- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from bearish to bullish within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment is high and price is near recent high, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “overbought” bias.
- When sentiment is low and price is near recent low, model undercorrects; add 0.5–2% to forecast to avoid “oversold” bias.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment >0.75 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be 1–2% higher than historical mean of same sentiment window.
